title: Nostalgia and sadness in his piano playing
summary: He says his playing tends toward darkness and he tries instead to lift spirits.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Does the nostalgia come out in your piano playing?

I think it’s gotten more and more the tendency to do that, but sometimes I have to control myself because I end up playing music that is too sad, sometimes I leave a bad impression. So I have to think about that you know, because if you start to try to put into music some of your emotion than unfortunately I might have the tendency to go toward a little bit of darkness and I don’t want to do that. You know? So I think maybe now more than ever we need to try to lift our spirits. We need to try to inspire other people for the best in the future to come you know. Because otherwise if we get into this loop of negativity it’s a disaster. Maybe I’m wrong. You know? Maybe I’m wrong.
I think the 97-year-old fellow who tunes into you every day will think you’re right.
